title: Pre-baked AI environments: layout authored by hand, art generated to it,collision measured off the pixels. Does this hold up?
author: kr0ng0

comments.author: DocHolidayPhD
comments.body: If you are working with 2D and images, the cost is likely quite small. Looking at what you're putting together also seems a bit over designed. Tell me, what are you actually aiming to do and why, in the big and small picture, as though you were speaking to a teenager.

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: from a neutral standpoint it does look kind of good. but everyone and their mama will know its ai generated. you cant do the same thing 3d with textures? i believe the "shadow thing when explosions/lights occur" will dramatically lower the appeal and increas ai hate in the finished product.

replies.author: kr0ng0
replies.body: The aim is to have environment with little bit old school style. Kind of like pre-baked scenes from Diablo or original Fallout. I have actually started with textures - the result was poor - far from this one. But this could be me and my artistic skills (read poor). I was always more Dev.

replies.author: lovable-fried-donut
replies.body: Yeah I’m not sure why you wouldn’t start with 3D and leverage an engine for the rest. Maybe a bit more detail on what you’re building and why, OP?

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Is image gen 2.5 still drifting for you? Seemed like that was the things this update was supposed to stop.

replies.author: kr0ng0
replies.body: Need to test the same prompt with GPT image 2.5 and compare the precision. Current pipeline is using Grok Imagine. Thanks for tip.
